addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

async def _run_kernel(arg: str, timeout: int) -> str:
    """One kernel command, its transcript, and nothing raised.

    The try lives here alone so the parser above it stays a straight line. A
    handler edge inside a scan is what Vox reads as a graph that does not
    validate, and it is also what makes such a function hard to follow.
    """
    runner = _MOMONADOS / "run_hosted_cmds.sh"
    raw = b""
    if runner.exists():
        proc = None
        try:
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                str(runner), arg, cwd=str(_MOMONADOS),
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE)
            so, se = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=timeout)
            raw = so + se
        except Exception:
            raw = b""
        finally:
            # wait_for cancels communicate(); it does NOT stop the child. Without
            # this the timed-out kernel call keeps running with its pipes held, one
            # orphan per churn node, and a live child at interpreter exit is what
            # asyncio's subprocess teardown aborts on. Kill, then REAP: an unwaited
            # child is a zombie, which is the same leak wearing a different name.
            if proc is not None and proc.returncode is None:
                try:
                    proc.kill()
                    await proc.wait()
                except Exception:
                    pass
    return _ANSI.sub("", raw.decode("utf-8", "replace"))

    """Ask the kernel which single-glyph insertions make `word` hold.

    Awaited rather than blocking: `subprocess.run` inside an async design loop
    stops the loop for the length of the call, which on a churn is once per node
    with nothing else able to proceed.

    out = await _run_kernel(f"insert {word}", timeout) if word else ""
    holds = [{"glyph": m.group(1), "position": int(m.group(2)), "word": m.group(3)}

    counted = [c for c in (_REPAIR_COUNT.search(l) for l in out.splitlines()) if c]
    counts = ({"hold": int(counted[0].group(1)), "tried": int(counted[0].group(2))}

def _build_provider_chain() -> List[Any]:
    """Return ordered list of live LLMProvider instances, skipping unavailable ones."""
    chain = []
    for name in _PROVIDER_CHAIN:
        try:
            p = get_llm_provider(name)

_P4RAMILL_DIR = Path("/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/p4rakernel/p4ramill")
_GATE_CHECK_DIR = _P4RAMILL_DIR / "Imscribing" / "Ob3ects" / "GateCheck"


async def _verify_lean_scaffold(artifact: "Ob3ectArtifact", slug: str) -> None:
    """
    The actual final gate: lean is scripture, not the Python heuristics
    upstream of it (generate_guided's Axiom A/B auto-correction, or
    generate_from_description's reasoning-text keyword grounding — both are
    wet-lab checks on an LLM's self-consistency, not a proof). Writes the
    artifact's own Lean scaffold to a real file under p4ramill and elaborates
    it for real with `lake env lean` — the same mechanism MoDoT's `TOOL: lean`
    uses. Sets artifact.grounding_status from the KERNEL's verdict, not the
    gate LLM's.

    No scaffold, no p4ramill checkout, or `lake` not on PATH → grounding_status
    stays whatever the gate step set it to, with lean_verified=None (not
    silently claimed as verified).
    """
    artifact.lean_verified = None
    artifact.lean_verification_output = ""
    if not artifact.lean_scaffold:
        return
    if not _P4RAMILL_DIR.is_dir():
        artifact.lean_verification_output = f"p4ramill not found at {_P4RAMILL_DIR} — could not elaborate."
        return

    _GATE_CHECK_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target = _GATE_CHECK_DIR / f"{slug}_gate_check.lean"
    target.write_text(artifact.lean_scaffold, encoding="utf-8")

    try:
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "lake", "env", "lean", str(target),
            cwd=str(_P4RAMILL_DIR),
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=180)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        artifact.lean_verification_output = "`lake` not found on PATH — could not elaborate."
        return
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        # Same reaping the kernel call needs: wait_for cancels communicate() but
        # leaves `lake` running. On a churn this fires once per node, so the
        # orphans accumulate for the whole walk and the last of them is still
        # alive when the interpreter tears down.
        try:
            proc.kill()
            await proc.wait()
        except Exception:
            pass
        artifact.lean_verification_output = "lake env lean timed out after 180s."
        return

    text = (stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace") + stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    body = "\n".join(l for l in text.splitlines() if "has local changes" not in l)
    n_err = body.count("error")
    artifact.lean_verification_output = body.strip()
    # The kernel's verdict is lean_verified, and ONLY lean_verified. grounding_status
    # belongs to the gated imscriber: overwriting it here let a scaffold that happened to
    # elaborate stamp "full" over a tuple the gate had (or would have) failed — the two
    # verdicts answer different questions and must not share a field.
    artifact.lean_verified = proc.returncode == 0 and n_err == 0

content.text:
Confirmed — no `setpgid`/`setsid` anywhere in the spawn path either. Found it.

**The bug:** `tools/server/server-models.cpp` force-kills a hung/stopped model-server child by calling `child_proc->terminate()`, which bottoms out in `vendor/sheredom/subprocess.h:1664` as `kill(process->child, 9)` — SIGKILL to that one PID, nothing else. The spawn path never calls `setpgid`/`setsid`, so a killed child's own children are never in a process group the killer controls.

That matters because a model-server child isn't a leaf: `server-tools.cpp` (line 1959, `spawn()`) has that same child launch and keep alive a persistent tools-runtime container process (`<engine> run --rm -i <image> sh`, auto-respawned if it dies — line 1944). When the router SIGKILLs the model-server child directly:

1. The direct child dies instantly.
2. The container process it spawned is never touched — it's reparented to PID 1 and keeps running.
3. It's invisible to `pkill -f llama-server`, since its command line is `docker run ...` / `podman run ...`, not `llama-server`.

That's exactly the "unkillable children" shape: under concurrent load, the router is force-killing and respawning model instances (`server-models.cpp:1066`, `:1113`, `:1145`, `:1268` — timeout, replace, unload-while-loading, all four paths route through the same bare `terminate()`), each kill can strand one more orphaned container process, and none of them answer to a kill targeted at the parent's name.

**Fix:** in `common/subproc.cpp`, spawn with `SUBPROCESS_OPTION_NONE` replaced by a new-process-group option (or call `setpgid(pid, pid)` right after fork in `subprocess_create`, POSIX path), and change `terminate()` to `kill(-process->child, 9)` (negative PID = kill the whole group) instead of `kill(process->child, 9)`.

Want me to write that patch?

Fix orphaned tools-runtime containers surviving a model-instance force-kill

The router force-kills a stuck or replaced model-server child through
common_subproc::terminate(), which only ever sent SIGKILL to that one pid.
subprocess_create() never put the child in its own process group, so a
grandchild it spawned and kept alive on its own — the tools-runtime
container process from server-tools.cpp, respawned if it dies — was never
in reach of that kill. It gets reparented to init and keeps running,
invisible to anything matching on our own argv, which is exactly the
"unkillable children" surviving under concurrent load I was seeing.

terminate() SIGKILL the whole group (negative pid) before the original
single-pid kill, so the group kill is in place even for a child created
before the setpgid could land.
EOF

content.content:
1	# IG_HARNESS — mOMonadOS-tool + Imscribing agentic harness
2	
3	![language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Python-3776AB?style=for-the-badge) ![tier](https://img.shields.io/badge/tier-O%E2%88%9E-8A2BE2?style=for-the-badge) ![μ∘δ](https://img.shields.io/badge/%CE%BC%E2%88%98%CE%B4-id-00A86B?style=for-the-badge) ![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-Unlicense-1A1A1A?style=for-the-badge)
4	
5	**Author:** Lando⊗⊙perator  
6	**Date:** 2026-08-23  
7	**Parent:** [MoDoT](../MoDoT) (formatting source) · [mOMonadOS](../mOMonadOS) (kernel substrate)
8	
9	---
10	
11	An agentic LLM harness with MoDoT's rigid formatting — B4 Belnap verdicts,
12	`[thought|X]` voice, `TOKEN:`/`COMPOSE:`/`CANONICAL:` composition, `prove:`
13	routing, Crystal FS context, Frobenius μ∘δ=id on every breath, CLINK L8
14	broadcast — with **two added foci**:
15	
16	1. **mOMonadOS-tool**: `MTOOL:` lines are grounded through the live hosted
17	   mOMonadOS kernel REPL (`ig`, `cycle`, `weight`, `banked`, `insert`,
18	   `trans`, `arev`, `decode`, `frob`, `aleph`, `shor`, `d12`, `fibqc`,
19	   `spine`, `vessel`, `vita`, `whoami`, `ruleset`, ...). The model says
20	   `MTOOL: ig mOMonadOS` and receives the kernel's real tuple + crystal
21	   address + IMASM word, not a narration.
22	2. **General imscribing-use**: `TOOL:`/`ACTION:` lines run the live IG tool
23	   corpus (54 tools: compute_distance, primitive_peel, crystal_decode,
24	   zfc_probe, aleph_encode, lookup_catalog, ouroborics, ...) through the
25	   shared IG_inquiry dispatcher.
26	
27	The shared machinery (B4, Token, CrystalFS, FrobeniusHarness, TokenComposer,
28	the ig_tools bridge) is imported from the MoDoT package — one manifold, no
29	fork. Only the mOMonadOS-tool bridge and the imscribing emphasis are new.
30	
31	## Quick Start
32	
33	```bash
34	cd IG_HARNESS
35	
36	# sanity: is the mOMonadOS bridge alive?
37	python3 -m ig_harness.agent --check-momos
38	
39	# one-shot question (LLM needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY or KILO_API_KEY / DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
40	python3 -m ig_harness.agent --ask "What is the type of consciousness?"
41	python3 -m ig_harness.agent --file my_question.md
42	
43	# interactive

# IG_HARNESS — mOMonadOS-tool + Imscribing agentic harness

![language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Python-3776AB?style=for-the-badge) ![tier](https://img.shields.io/badge/tier-O%E2%88%9E-8A2BE2?style=for-the-badge) ![μ∘δ](https://img.shields.io/badge/%CE%BC%E2%88%98%CE%B4-id-00A86B?style=for-the-badge) ![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-Unlicense-1A1A1A?style=for-the-badge)

**Author:** Lando⊗⊙perator  
**Date:** 2026-08-23  
**Parent:** [MoDoT](../MoDoT) (formatting source) · [mOMonadOS](../mOMonadOS) (kernel substrate)

---

An agentic LLM harness with MoDoT's rigid formatting — B4 Belnap verdicts,
`[thought|X]` voice, `TOKEN:`/`COMPOSE:`/`CANONICAL:` composition, `prove:`
routing, Crystal FS context, Frobenius μ∘δ=id on every breath, CLINK L8
broadcast — with **two added foci**:

1. **mOMonadOS-tool**: `MTOOL:` lines are grounded through the live hosted
   mOMonadOS kernel REPL (`ig`, `cycle`, `weight`, `banked`, `insert`,
   `trans`, `arev`, `decode`, `frob`, `aleph`, `shor`, `d12`, `fibqc`,
   `spine`, `vessel`, `vita`, `whoami`, `ruleset`, ...). The model says
   `MTOOL: ig mOMonadOS` and receives the kernel's real tuple + crystal
   address + IMASM word, not a narration.
2. **General imscribing-use**: `TOOL:`/`ACTION:` lines run the live IG tool
   corpus (54 tools: compute_distance, primitive_peel, crystal_decode,
   zfc_probe, aleph_encode, lookup_catalog, ouroborics, ...) through the
   shared IG_inquiry dispatcher.

The shared machinery (B4, Token, CrystalFS, FrobeniusHarness, TokenComposer,
the ig_tools bridge) is imported from the MoDoT package — one manifold, no
fork. Only the mOMonadOS-tool bridge and the imscribing emphasis are new.

## Quick Start

```bash
cd IG_HARNESS

# sanity: is the mOMonadOS bridge alive?
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --check-momos

# one-shot question (LLM needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY or KILO_API_KEY / DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --ask "What is the type of consciousness?"
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --file my_question.md

# interactive
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --interactive

# dry-run: no LLM, test the kernel + Crystal FS + bridges
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --cycles 2 --dry-run --verbose

# Crystal FS
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --stats
python3 -m ig_harness.agent --reset --interactive

# model routing (same env as MoDoT)
IG_MODEL=deepseek:deepseek-reasoner python3 -m ig_harness.agent --ask "..."
```

## The breath loop

THINK → ACT → OBSERVE → UPDATE, then kernel run_cycle, then CLINK L8
broadcast. In ACT, three rigid line kinds are grounded:

| line | backend | example |
|------|---------|---------|
| `MTOOL: <cmd>` | hosted mOMonadOS kernel REPL | `MTOOL: ig mOMonadOS` |
| `TOOL: <name> <args>` | live IG_inquiry dispatcher | `TOOL: compute_distance a b` |
| `TOKEN:`/`COMPOSE:`/`CANONICAL:` | shared modot.composer | `COMPOSE: canonical I_Dialetheic_Bootstrap` |

The model ends its answer with `[thought|T|F|B|N]`; kernel-owned record types
(`[selectivity|..]`, `[vessel|..]`, `[spine|..]`, `[update|..]`,
`[broadcast|..]`) are stripped from ingest so the model cannot fabricate
authoritative verdicts.

## Directory

```
IG_HARNESS/
├── ig_harness/
│   ├── agent.py        # breath loop, B4, CrystalFS, Frobenius, LLM, CLI
│   ├── momos.py        # mOMonadOS-tool bridge (hosted kernel REPL)
│   └── __init__.py
├── crystal_fs/         # records.jsonl + broadcast_log.jsonl
├── pyproject.toml
└── README.md
```

## mOMonadOS-tool allowlist

The bridge refuses any verb outside the allowlist (no arbitrary shell). Run
`python3 -m ig_harness.agent --list-mtools` for the live list.

## Honest notes

- MTOOL output is the hosted kernel's real REPL answer; a refused/absent
  verb returns `[refused]`/`[unavailable]`, never a fake.
- Dry-run mode exercises the full loop with no API calls.
- The kernel mirror in `agent.py` is a thin Python program loop; the real
  kernel is the Rust mOMonadOS binary the bridge talks to.

    def breathe(self, user_input=None, max_cycles=1):
        """Run max_cycles user-visible turns. A turn is one or more full
        THINK -> ACT -> OBSERVE -> UPDATE passes: it keeps cycling on its
        own, capped at MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS, for as long as THINK keeps proposing
        tool_calls, and ends the moment THINK answers with none. Every round
        is a real TAOU pass -- tool execution happens in ACT, never inside
        THINK -- so the breath loop's own cadence is what drives multi-round
        tool use, not a private loop hidden inside one phase."""
        results = []
        turns_done = 0
        pending_input = user_input
        while turns_done < max_cycles:
            # kernel.halted is NOT a stop condition for conversation turns:
            # MomonadosKernel.run_cycle() below latches it permanently True
            # after its very first call, ever, on this agent instance (it
            # loops step() to completion internally in one shot). Gating
            # on it here killed every turn after the first outright --
            # breathe() returned instantly with zero phase-entries and the
            # interactive loop looked like it had stopped accepting input.
            turn_input = pending_input
            pending_input = None
            for _round in range(self.MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS):
                self.cycle_count += 1
                thought = self._think(turn_input)

                action = self._act(thought)
                results.append(("ACT", action))
                observation = self._observe(action)
                results.append(("OBSERVE", observation))
                update = self._update(thought, action, observation)
                results.append(("UPDATE", update))
                self.kernel.run_cycle()
                self._broadcast()
                turn_input = None
                if not thought.get("tool_calls"):
                    break
            turns_done += 1
        return results

content.text:
Found it. All three of the CLI's print loops (interactive, `--ask`/`--file`, and the plain cycles loop) only ever check `if phase == "THINK"` — the `("ACT", action)` entries `breathe()` returns, which are the only place `action["calls"]` (the real per-tool grounded output strings from `_handle_mtool`/`_handle_ig_tool`/`_run_tool_call`) live, are never printed anywhere. The only tool-related thing that reaches the terminal is the one-line `[tool_call] {names}` in `_infer_stream` (line 258) — just the tool names, not their results. Everything else is silently discarded after being written into Crystal FS.

`--verbose` doesn't fix it either — its ACT branch (line 987-990) also filters to `phase == "THINK"` only.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

---
name: m2_torus_native_toroidal_llm
description: m2_torus — the trunk trains now; candle's fused rms_norm was dropping the gradient, and the corpus is the ob3ect opcode sequences
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Grammar-native toroidal LM in `daydr33m/m2_torus`, trained as a masked-ring
IMASM denoiser. As of 2026-08-13 it works: **held-out denoise 60.4% against 8.3%
chance, 44 of 64 filled val rings Closed**, loss 0.87 (ln 12 = 2.485).

**The trunk was frozen for every run before that.** `candle_nn::rms_norm` carries
no gradient back to what feeds it. Every layer parameter sits behind a norm —
fork and fuse behind `norm_attn`, both ENGAGR arms and `ff_fuse` behind
`norm_ff` — so all 48 held their initial value to eight decimals while the
residual `x + f(norm(x))` still carried gradient to the embedding through its
`x` term. Loss fell, the trunk looked trained, and six layers of random
projection sat in the middle. Every number before the fix (15.1%, 17.1%, 21.3%,
23.3%) was an embedding and a tied head doing unigram statistics. The fix is an
explicit `Rms` module in `model.rs`: `x * rsqrt(mean(x²)+eps) * weight`.

Diagnosis that found it: with `--gate-lambda 0` the printed gate never moved at
all, because `gate_penalty` — which measures ‖WᵀW−I‖² on fork and fuse, NOT on
the gate — was the only gradient those two ever got. Printing ‖W‖² per parameter
showed embed moving and every layer weight constant. If a metric is bit-identical
across steps, the parameter is not being trained; check before reading the curve.

**The corpus is the ob3ect opcode sequences.** `ob3ect/digital/*/​*_ob3ect.json`
carries `phases.phase_4.steps`, an ordered opcode list per ob3ect; the twelve
opcodes are the twelve marks (VINIT ⊢, TANCH ⊣, AFWD >, AREV <, CLINK ⋈,
EVALT ⊤, FSPLIT ∈, FFUSE ∋, IMSCRIB ⊙, EVALF ⊥, ENGAGR ⊞, IFIX ◻). 1703
sequences, 1277 distinct, lengths 3..114 → `ob3ect_words.txt`. The old
`imasm_words.txt` (1502 rings of unrecorded provenance) was the ceiling: it
plateaued at 17% no matter the steps. Do NOT look for words in the ob3ect SVGs —
only 26 of 1340 carry one, and `grounded_tuple` in the JSON is a 12-VALUE
Shavian tuple, a different object from the word.

`train.rs` takes every knob on the command line now (`--lr --ring --batch
--mask-frac --gate-lambda --seed --d-model --layers --heads --ff-mult --sigma0
--causal --val-frac --log-every`), and accepts variable-length rings: longer
than the window wraps, shorter pads with the padding excluded from masking and
from the loss. Best so far: `--lr 9e-4 --ring 16`, 10k steps.

Open: the gate penalty now RISES after step ~2600 (0.0333 → 0.0534) — the trunk
trades μ∘δ=id deviation for task performance once it can actually learn. That
exchange rate is what `--gate-lambda` sets. See [[the_forty_nine]].

content.text:
That ob3ect's `phase_4.steps` is a literal architecture spec, not just a corpus entry. Read straight through, it's one transformer block where the difference from a standard one is exact and buildable:

- Standard attention: `∈` splits into heads, each head computes a single softmax-normalized score per key (affirm and reject get collapsed into one number).
- This spec: `∈` splits, `⊤` computes the affirm arm, `⊥` computes the reject arm **separately**, `⊞` holds both without resolving them into one scalar (genuine Belnap B, not a softmax blend), then `∋` fuses heads while still carrying that unresolved pair.

Same shape repeats for the feed-forward block (`∈`/`⊤`/`⊥`/`⊞`/`∋` at steps 11–15) as an MoE split: experts compute affirm/reject in parallel, held at B, fused without forcing a single winner.

So what it says to build is a **B4 attention layer**: per (query, key) pair, keep two independent scores — affirm strength and reject strength — instead of one softmax weight, classify each as T/F/B/N off the Belnap lattice, and only fuse heads/experts after that, never before. That's a real, different attention mechanism from anything in `m2_torus` today, which trains a ring-denoiser *on* these opcode sequences as corpus but doesn't implement what this one describes.

Before I write Rust: is this meant to land inside `daydr33m/m2_torus` as a new layer type alongside the existing trunk, or as its own standalone module you're testing separately?

# (F) SEPARATELY, holds both without resolving them to one softmax weight

# dialetheic_llm

Built from `ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm_ob3ect.json`,
`phases.phase_4.steps` — read as a build order, not a description.

A standard transformer computes attention by masking disallowed (future) key
positions to `-inf` and taking one softmax. The affirm/reject arms — `⊤`/`⊥`
in the spec — collapse into a single number at that step; whatever the reject
arm would have said is never computed. This model computes both arms as real
tensors (`DialetheicAttention` in `src/lib.rs`), concatenates them per head
(the `⊞` hold), and only reduces dimension afterward through a learned
projection (the `∋` fuse). The feed-forward block repeats the same shape as
two always-on experts (`affirm_in/out`, `reject_in/out`) blended by a learned
per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side — no top-1 MoE
routing, which would reintroduce the same collapse.

## Layout

- `src/lib.rs` — `DialetheicAttention`, `DialetheicFfn`, `Block`, `DialetheicLlm`.
- `src/bin/train.rs` — trains on newline-separated glyph rings (steps 19-23:
  backward, gradient chain via candle autodiff, a printed `|W|`/`d|W|` as the
  model's own weight-update readback, checkpoint save as the anchor).
- `src/bin/gen.rs` — autoregressive sampling.

## Vocabulary

Twelve marks, checked against the on-disk corpus rather than assumed:
`⊢ ⊣ > < ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. The corpus at
`daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt` spells AFWD/AREV as ASCII `>`/`<`, not
≻/≺ — `id_of`/`GLYPHS` match that, not the mark table, so nothing gets
silently dropped by `encode()`.

## Run

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/dl-train ../daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt 2000 dialetheic.safetensors
./target/release/dl-gen dialetheic.safetensors "⊢" 30
```

Confirmed live: 2000 steps on the 1703-ring corpus, loss falls from chance
(ln 12 ≈ 2.48) to ~1.3-2.0, generation produces well-formed short rings
(`⊢…⊣` bracketing, balanced `∈…∋`) from a bare `⊢` seed.

## Not built

Step 18 of the spec ("fix the key-value pairs into the KV cache as a
permanent record") — `gen.rs` recomputes the full forward pass on every
sampled glyph instead of caching. Correct, not incremental.

Not a git repo, nothing to commit — the build lives in `~/imsgct/dialetheic_llm`.

**Built `dialetheic_llm` from scratch**, a Rust/candle crate implementing exactly what `phase_4.steps` specifies:

- **`DialetheicAttention`** — computes the affirm arm (causal softmax) and reject arm (softmax over the future, the positions standard attention masks to `-inf` and discards) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head (the `⊞` hold), then a single learned projection fuses them to `d_model` (the `∋` step). Found and fixed a real NaN bug along the way: the last sequence position has no future, so its reject-arm softmax was `0/0` before the row mask ever got a chance to zero it.
- **`DialetheicFfn`** — two always-on experts (never top-1 routed, which would reintroduce the same collapse) blended by a per-token sigmoid gate.
- **`train.rs`** — trains on the corpus already sitting at `daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt`. Also caught and fixed a vocabulary bug: the corpus spells AFWD/AREV as ASCII `>`/`<`, not `≻`/`≺` — checked the actual file rather than assuming from the mark table, which would have silently dropped every occurrence.
- **`gen.rs`** — autoregressive sampling, full-recompute (no KV cache yet — that's step 18 of the spec, left open and named in the README, not built).

Confirmed live: 2000 steps on the 1703-ring corpus, loss falls from chance (ln 12 ≈ 2.48) to ~1.3–2.0, no NaN. Generation from a bare `⊢` seed produces well-formed rings with proper `⊢…⊣` bracketing and balanced `∈…∋`.

p4radice: a dialetheic-attention transformer built from an ob3ect spec

Built dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm's phase_4.steps straight, reading
it as a build order instead of a description. Standard attention masks the
future to -inf before its one softmax, so the reject arm never exists as a
value. Here the affirm arm and reject arm are both computed, held
concatenated (the spec's ⊞ step), and only fused down through a learned
projection afterward (∋) — so the network decides what the contradiction
means instead of the architecture erasing half of it in advance. The
feed-forward block carries the same shape as two always-on experts blended by
a per-token gate, never top-1 routed.

Confirmed live: 2000 steps on the 1703-ring ob3ect corpus, loss falls from
chance to ~1.3-2.0 with no NaN once two real bugs were caught and fixed —
the last position's empty reject-softmax was 0/0 before its row mask ever
ran, and the vocabulary was checked against the actual on-disk corpus
(AFWD/AREV spelled as ASCII >/< there, not ≻/≺). Generation from a bare ⊢
produces well-formed rings with real ⊢…⊣ bracketing and balanced ∈…∋.

KV-cache incremental decode (the spec's step 18) is not built; gen.rs
recomputes the full prefix every step instead.
EOF

# p4radice

Built from `ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm_ob3ect.json`,
`phases.phase_4.steps` — read as a build order, not a description.

A standard transformer computes attention by masking disallowed (future) key
positions to `-inf` and taking one softmax. The affirm/reject arms — `⊤`/`⊥`
in the spec — collapse into a single number at that step; whatever the reject
arm would have said is never computed. This model computes both arms as real
tensors (`DialetheicAttention` in `src/lib.rs`), concatenates them per head
(the `⊞` hold), and only reduces dimension afterward through a learned
projection (the `∋` fuse). The feed-forward block repeats the same shape as
two always-on experts (`affirm_in/out`, `reject_in/out`) blended by a learned
per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side — no top-1 MoE
routing, which would reintroduce the same collapse.

## Layout

- `src/lib.rs` — `DialetheicAttention`, `DialetheicFfn`, `Block`, `DialetheicLlm`.
- `src/bin/train.rs` — trains on newline-separated glyph rings (steps 19-23:
  backward, gradient chain via candle autodiff, a printed `|W|`/`d|W|` as the
  model's own weight-update readback, checkpoint save as the anchor).
- `src/bin/gen.rs` — autoregressive sampling.

## Vocabulary

Twelve marks, checked against the on-disk corpus rather than assumed:
`⊢ ⊣ > < ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. The corpus at
`daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt` spells AFWD/AREV as ASCII `>`/`<`, not
≻/≺ — `id_of`/`GLYPHS` match that, not the mark table, so nothing gets
silently dropped by `encode()`.

## Run

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/dl-train ../daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt 2000 p4radice.safetensors
./target/release/dl-gen p4radice.safetensors "⊢" 30
```

Confirmed live: 2000 steps on the 1703-ring corpus, loss falls from chance
(ln 12 ≈ 2.48) to ~1.3-2.0, generation produces well-formed short rings
(`⊢…⊣` bracketing, balanced `∈…∋`) from a bare `⊢` seed.

## Not built

Step 18 of the spec ("fix the key-value pairs into the KV cache as a
permanent record") — `gen.rs` recomputes the full forward pass on every
sampled glyph instead of caching. Correct, not incremental.

# Running p4radice

## Build

```
cargo build --release
```

CUDA build: `cargo build --release --features cuda`

## Train

```
./target/release/p4-train <corpus.txt> <steps> <checkpoint.safetensors>
```

All three arguments are optional and default to the ob3ect corpus already on
disk, 2000 steps, and `p4radice.safetensors` in this directory:

```
./target/release/p4-train

# m2_torus

**What it is.** A language model whose architecture is the Imscribing Grammar,
built from zero in native Rust — no pretrained weights. Catalog-crystal
embeddings, winding positions, toroidal (circulant ring + content) attention held
to μ∘δ = id, the ENGAGR held-dual feed-forward, and the kernel's own closure
verdict as the gate.

**What it does.** Trains as a masked-ring IMASM denoiser over the twelve marks
and produces rings the kernel (`imasm_core::word_verdict`) certifies as closed.
Host trains → `m2-bake` flattens to an `M2TO` f32 blob → (planned) mOMonadOS runs
it native no_std.

**Why it matters.** The ring the toroidal kernel imposes is native to m⊙²; this
model is built ON that ring and closes by construction, rather than approximating
IMASM with a foreign transformer and checking it afterwards.

**How to use it.**
```
cargo test                                 # 6 architecture tests
cargo build --release
./target/release/m2-train 2000             # train, report denoising + kernel closures
./target/release/m2-gen torus_trunk.safetensors 10   # fill rings, print verdicts
./target/release/m2-bake torus_trunk.safetensors torus_weights.bin
```
Located at `~/imsgct/daydr33m/m2_torus/`. Full reference: `ig-docs/m2_torus_native_toroidal_llm.md`.

## GPU (CUDA)

The default `/usr/bin/nvcc` is CUDA 11.5 — too old for the 4070 (sm_89) — so a
plain `--features cuda` build fails and silently falls back to CPU. This crate
pins the 12.4 toolkit in `.cargo/config.toml`, so:

```
cargo build --release --features cuda        # builds candle's CUDA kernels with 12.4
source .cargo_cuda_env.sh                     # runtime lib path + CUDA_COMPUTE_CAP
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./target/release/m2-train 4000    # 0 = RTX 4070, ~32 steps/s
# or: ./run-gpu.sh ./target/release/m2-train 4000
```

Without `--features cuda` (or on a CPU-only box) it runs on CPU unchanged.

# p4radice

**What it is.** A transformer built from `ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm`'s
`phase_4.steps`, read as a build order rather than a description of an
existing architecture. Every ordinary transformer computes attention by
masking the future to `-inf` and taking one softmax, so the affirm and reject
arms — what a position argues FOR and what it argues AGAINST — collapse into
a single number at that step, and the reject arm never exists as a value
anywhere. `p4radice` computes both arms for real, holds them concatenated,
and only reduces dimension afterward through a learned projection, so the
network decides what a contradiction means instead of the architecture
erasing half of it before the network ever sees it. The feed-forward block
carries the same shape: two experts, both always on, blended by a per-token
gate that never fully zeroes either side.

**What it does.** Trains as a causal next-glyph model over the twelve marks,
on the same 1703-ring `ob3ect_words.txt` corpus `m2_torus` uses. Confirmed
live at 2000 steps: loss falls from chance (ln 12 ≈ 2.48) to ~1.3-2.0 with no
NaN, and generation from a bare `⊢` produces well-formed rings — real `⊢…⊣`
bracketing, balanced `∈…∋` — rather than noise.

**Why it matters.** It is a real, checkable answer to whether "hold the
contradiction instead of resolving it" is buildable as an actual attention
mechanism, not just a description of one. Two bugs turned up building it and
are worth knowing about going in: the last sequence position has no future,
so its reject-arm softmax is `0/0` before any mask can zero it, and the
on-disk corpus spells AFWD/AREV as ASCII `>`/`<`, not `≻`/`≺` — checked
directly rather than assumed from the mark table.

**How to use it.** See `GUIDE.md` — build, train, generate, and the full
architecture breakdown. Located at `~/imsgct/p4radice/`.

  --n-head n        attention heads                  (4)
  --d-ff n          feed-forward width                (256)
  --n-layer n       depth                            (4)
  --max-len n       max sequence length               (128)
```

Example sweep:

```
./target/release/p4-train --d-model 128 --n-head 8 --n-layer 6 --batch 8 --lr 1e-4 --steps 5000 --out big.safetensors
```

The corpus file is newline-separated glyph rings, each built from the twelve
marks. Prints loss and `|W|`/`d|W|` (the weight-norm and its change) every
`--log-every` steps, saves the checkpoint at the end.

```
./target/release/p4-gen [flags]
./target/release/p4-gen --help
```

```
  --ckpt F          checkpoint path                  (p4radice.safetensors)
  --seed W          seed word, built from the twelve glyphs   (⊢)
  --n-gen n         glyphs to sample                 (40)

```

into the wrong-shaped tensors and candle errors on the first size that
disagrees. Samples autoregressively from the seed word until it emits `⊣`
or hits `--n-gen`. Recomputes the full prefix every step — no KV cache yet.

# Running p4radice

## Build

```
cargo build --release
```

CUDA build: `cargo build --release --features cuda`

## Train

```
./target/release/p4-train <corpus.txt> <steps> <checkpoint.safetensors>
```

All three arguments are optional and default to the ob3ect corpus already on
disk, 2000 steps, and `p4radice.safetensors` in this directory:

```
./target/release/p4-train
./target/release/p4-train ../daydr33m/m2_torus/ob3ect_words.txt 2000 p4radice.safetensors
```

The corpus file is newline-separated glyph rings, each built from the twelve
marks. Prints loss and `|W|`/`d|W|` (the weight-norm and its change) every
100 steps, saves the checkpoint at the end.

## Generate

```
./target/release/p4-gen <checkpoint.safetensors> <seed> <n_glyphs>
./target/release/p4-gen p4radice.safetensors "⊢" 30
```

Samples autoregressively from the seed word until it emits `⊣` or hits
`n_glyphs`. Recomputes the full prefix every step — no KV cache yet.

## Vocabulary

Twelve marks, checked against the on-disk corpus rather than the mark table:
`⊢ ⊣ > < ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. AFWD/AREV are ASCII `>`/`<` here, not ≻/≺,
because that is what `ob3ect_words.txt` actually contains.

## What the architecture does

`src/lib.rs`:

- `DialetheicAttention` — computes an affirm arm (ordinary causal softmax)
  and a reject arm (softmax over exactly the future positions affirm was
  masked from) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head, then
  fuses with one learned projection back to `d_model`. Standard attention
  never computes the reject arm at all — it masks those logits to `-inf`
  before its one softmax runs.
- `DialetheicFfn` — two always-on experts (never top-1 routed) blended by a
  per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side.
- `Block` / `DialetheicLlm` — the usual residual + layernorm stack around
  both, plus token/position embeddings and an output head.

Not built: incremental KV-cache decode (spec step 18). `gen.rs` stands in
for it by recomputing the full sequence each step.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.

  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.

  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of

- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Running p4radice

## Build

```
cargo build --release
```

CUDA build: `cargo build --release --features cuda`

## Train

```
./target/release/p4-train [flags]
./target/release/p4-train --help
```

Nothing is hardcoded — every knob is a flag, all with defaults:

```
  --corpus F        newline-separated glyph rings   (ob3ect_words.txt)
  --out F           checkpoint path                 (p4radice.safetensors)
  --steps n         training steps                  (2000)
  --lr F            AdamW learning rate              (3e-4)
  --batch n         rings per step                   (1)
  --seed n          RNG seed                         (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
  --log-every n     steps between log lines          (100)
  --d-model n       model width                      (64)
  --n-head n        attention heads                  (4)
  --d-ff n          feed-forward width                (256)
  --n-layer n       depth                            (4)
  --max-len n       max sequence length               (128)
```

Example sweep:

```
./target/release/p4-train --d-model 128 --n-head 8 --n-layer 6 --batch 8 --lr 1e-4 --steps 5000 --out big.safetensors
```

The corpus file is newline-separated glyph rings, each built from the twelve
marks. Prints loss and `|W|`/`d|W|` (the weight-norm and its change) every
`--log-every` steps, saves the checkpoint at the end.

## Generate

```
./target/release/p4-gen [flags]
./target/release/p4-gen --help
```

```
  --ckpt F          checkpoint path                  (p4radice.safetensors)
  --seed W          seed word, built from the twelve glyphs   (⊢)
  --n-gen n         glyphs to sample                 (40)
  --d-model / --n-head / --d-ff / --n-layer / --max-len   must match training
```

The five architecture flags are not stored in the `.safetensors` file, so
they must match whatever `p4-train` was run with — a mismatch loads weights
into the wrong-shaped tensors and candle errors on the first size that
disagrees. Samples autoregressively from the seed word until it emits `⊣`
or hits `--n-gen`. Recomputes the full prefix every step — no KV cache yet.

## Vocabulary

Twelve marks, checked against the on-disk corpus rather than the mark table:
`⊢ ⊣ > < ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. AFWD/AREV are ASCII `>`/`<` here, not ≻/≺,
because that is what `ob3ect_words.txt` actually contains.

## What the architecture does

`src/lib.rs`:

- `DialetheicAttention` — computes an affirm arm (ordinary causal softmax)
  and a reject arm (softmax over exactly the future positions affirm was
  masked from) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head, then
  fuses with one learned projection back to `d_model`. Standard attention
  never computes the reject arm at all — it masks those logits to `-inf`
  before its one softmax runs.
- `DialetheicFfn` — two always-on experts (never top-1 routed) blended by a
  per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side.
- `Block` / `DialetheicLlm` — the usual residual + layernorm stack around
  both, plus token/position embeddings and an output head.

Not built: incremental KV-cache decode (spec step 18). `gen.rs` stands in
for it by recomputing the full sequence each step.

Raise default batch from 1 to 8, evidenced live

with lr raised to 9e-4 doesn't fix it (1.97, still bouncing), batch=32

just more wall-clock for a smoother gradient. batch=8 gets most of the

at batch=8, so there's nothing to justify moving it.

Architecture defaults (d-model/n-head/d-ff/n-layer/max-len) are untouched:
no comparison run backs a different choice, so nothing changed there.
EOF

content.text:
No — everything tracked so far (loss, `|W|`/`d|W|`) is generic language-model health. None of it measures whether training is actually keeping the model dialetheic, versus quietly collapsing back to an ordinary transformer that happens to have extra unused parameters.

Two concrete failure modes loss can't see:

1. **The FFN gate collapsing.** `DialetheicFfn`'s gate `g = sigmoid(gate(x))` is supposed to keep both experts live. If training pushes `g` toward 0 or 1 everywhere, one expert stops mattering and the "always both, never top-1" design is dead in practice even though the code still runs it.
2. **The attention fuse zeroing the reject arm.** `DialetheicAttention.o` is one linear layer over `[affirm ++ reject]`. If its weight columns reading from the reject half shrink toward zero relative to the affirm half, the reject arm is computed every step and then discarded — the model becomes a standard causal transformer with dead weight attached, not a paraconsistent one.

Both are checkable without new theory — read `gate`'s output distribution over a batch, and compare the norm of `o`'s weight columns split by affirm-half vs reject-half. A model training correctly should keep the gate spread out (not saturated) and keep both weight-column blocks comparably scaled, not shrinking one toward zero.

Want me to add that instrumentation to `train.rs` — printed alongside loss — so we can see straight away whether the current run is doing this or already collapsing?

content.text:
Checked before assuming — ran the actual entropy numbers on the corpus. My first guess was wrong: what follows `⊞` in the real data is *less* ambiguous (2.77 bits) than the average next-glyph position (3.44 bits, over 20,908 positions) — `⊞` is usually followed by `∋` (about a third of the time). So "stay uncertain right after `⊞`" isn't a real target; the data doesn't support it.

The positive signature has to be about branching in general, not about `⊞` specifically. Every position in the corpus has some number of glyphs that legally follow it there — some contexts are near-deterministic, some genuinely fork several ways. The good trend to aim for:

**The gate should track the data's own uncertainty, and that tracking should get tighter as training goes on** — at low-branching positions (only one or two glyphs ever follow, in the real corpus) the FFN gate `g` should move toward a decisive value (near 0 or 1: correctly resolved, no reason to hold two arms open when the data isn't actually contradictory there). At high-branching positions (several glyphs genuinely compete) `g` should sit nearer 0.5 and the reject arm's contribution should carry real weight, because that's where holding two arms open is earning its keep. What I'd want to see as training proceeds isn't gate values converging to any fixed number — it's the *correlation* between local branching factor and gate decisiveness getting stronger.

That's checkable: compute each corpus position's real branching factor once (offline, from the corpus itself), then during training log the correlation between that and the live gate value on the same positions.

Want me to build that — a branching-factor precompute plus the correlation printed alongside loss?

# Running p4radice

## Build

```
cargo build --release
```

CUDA build: `cargo build --release --features cuda`

## Train

```
./target/release/p4-train [flags]
./target/release/p4-train --help
```

Nothing is hardcoded — every knob is a flag, all with defaults:

```
  --corpus F        newline-separated glyph rings   (ob3ect_words.txt)
  --out F           checkpoint path                 (p4radice.safetensors)
  --steps n         training steps                  (2000)
  --lr F            AdamW learning rate              (3e-4)
  --batch n         rings per step                   (8)
  --seed n          RNG seed                         (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
  --log-every n     steps between log lines          (100)
  --d-model n       model width                      (64)
  --n-head n        attention heads                  (4)
  --d-ff n          feed-forward width                (256)
  --n-layer n       depth                            (4)
  --max-len n       max sequence length               (128)
```

Example sweep:

```
./target/release/p4-train --d-model 128 --n-head 8 --n-layer 6 --batch 8 --lr 1e-4 --steps 5000 --out big.safetensors
```

The corpus file is newline-separated glyph rings, each built from the twelve
marks. Prints loss and `|W|`/`d|W|` (the weight-norm and its change) every
`--log-every` steps, saves the checkpoint at the end.

## Generate

```
./target/release/p4-gen [flags]
./target/release/p4-gen --help
```

```
  --ckpt F          checkpoint path                  (p4radice.safetensors)
  --seed W          seed word, built from the twelve glyphs   (⊢)
  --n-gen n         glyphs to sample                 (40)
  --d-model / --n-head / --d-ff / --n-layer / --max-len   must match training
```

The five architecture flags are not stored in the `.safetensors` file, so
they must match whatever `p4-train` was run with — a mismatch loads weights
into the wrong-shaped tensors and candle errors on the first size that
disagrees. Samples autoregressively from the seed word until it emits `⊣`
or hits `--n-gen`. Recomputes the full prefix every step — no KV cache yet.

## Vocabulary

Twelve marks, checked against the on-disk corpus rather than the mark table:
`⊢ ⊣ > < ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. AFWD/AREV are ASCII `>`/`<` here, not ≻/≺,
because that is what `ob3ect_words.txt` actually contains.

## What the architecture does

`src/lib.rs`:

- `DialetheicAttention` — computes an affirm arm (ordinary causal softmax)
  and a reject arm (softmax over exactly the future positions affirm was
  masked from) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head, then

  per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side.
- `Block` / `DialetheicLlm` — the usual residual + layernorm stack around
  both, plus token/position embeddings and an output head.

for it by recomputing the full sequence each step.

# p4radice

**What it is.** A transformer built from `ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm`'s
`phase_4.steps`, read as a build order rather than a description of an
existing architecture. Every ordinary transformer computes attention by
masking the future to `-inf` and taking one softmax, so the affirm and reject
arms — what a position argues FOR and what it argues AGAINST — collapse into
a single number at that step, and the reject arm never exists as a value
anywhere. `p4radice` computes both arms for real, holds them concatenated,
and only reduces dimension afterward through a learned projection, so the
network decides what a contradiction means instead of the architecture
erasing half of it before the network ever sees it. The feed-forward block
carries the same shape: two experts, both always on, blended by a per-token
gate that never fully zeroes either side.

**What it does.** Trains as a causal next-glyph model over the twelve marks,
on the same 1703-ring `ob3ect_words.txt` corpus `m2_torus` uses. Confirmed
live at 2000 steps: loss falls from chance (ln 12 ≈ 2.48) to ~1.3-2.0 with no
NaN, and generation from a bare `⊢` produces well-formed rings — real `⊢…⊣`
bracketing, balanced `∈…∋` — rather than noise.

**Why it matters.** It is a real, checkable answer to whether "hold the
contradiction instead of resolving it" is buildable as an actual attention
mechanism, not just a description of one. Two bugs turned up building it and
are worth knowing about going in: the last sequence position has no future,
so its reject-arm softmax is `0/0` before any mask can zero it, and the
on-disk corpus spells AFWD/AREV as ASCII `>`/`<`, not `≻`/`≺` — checked
directly rather than assumed from the mark table.

**How to use it.** See `GUIDE.md` — build, train, generate, and the full
architecture breakdown. Located at `~/imsgct/p4radice/`.

That's the real answer, from the kernel's own `word_verdict`, run against every ring in the corpus `p4radice` actually trains on:

| verdict | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| B (paradox held) | 1378 | 81% |
| T (clean close) | 308 | 18% |
| N (void/identity) | 13 | <1% |
| F | 4 | <1% |

The training target is overwhelmingly B by the kernel's own check, not just by the ob3ect's design notes. That gives a real, Grammar-grounded target for "proper dialetheic training": as `p4radice` trains, the words it generates should trend toward that same ~81% B / 18% T split, not toward 100% T (over-resolving every contradiction the corpus actually holds) and not toward N/F (malformed output, a different failure than collapse).

That's checkable with the same instrument, no new invented statistic — run `p4-gen` at each checkpoint, feed the samples through this `check_corpus` binary, and watch the B-share converge toward 81% as loss falls. Want that wired into `train.rs` as a periodic check, generating a few samples every N steps and reporting their verdict split alongside loss?

content.text:
Correct — checked the code, not assumed. Each corpus line is loaded once (`words: Vec<Vec<usize>>` from the raw file) and every training step just picks one of those fixed sequences and slices `w[..n]` from its start. No rotation ever happens — every word is presented in whatever single cut it was written in on disk, every step, for the whole run.

That matters given `weight`'s own rule: a landing is frame-bound, only the verdict/topology hold across the ring's whole orbit. Training only ever sees one frame per ring, so the model can't be learning anything about the other cuts of the same ring — it's learning one fixed linearization per ring, not the ring itself.

content.text:
What's shown: repeated `p4-gen` runs from a bare `⊢` or `⊙` seed (correctly stopping fast on a sampled `⊣`, giving short well-formed rings), then several runs seeded with an *already-closed* word (one that already ends in `⊣`, itself output from a prior run) — and those keep generating past the seed's own `⊣`, appending a whole second ring onto the end (`⊙∈≻≺⋈∈⊤⊞≻∋⊣⊙⊤⊣`, `…⊣⊙≺⋈≺◻⊣⊙∈∋∋⊙⊞∋⊥⊣`, etc.).

That's `gen.rs`'s stop condition: it only breaks when a *newly sampled* glyph is `⊣` (`src/bin/gen.rs`, the `if glyph_of(next) == '⊣' { break; }` line). If the seed you pass already contains a `⊣`, nothing checks that — the loop has no idea the seed was already closed, so it just keeps sampling from where the seed left off and can produce a second closed ring chained onto the first.

Do you want seeding with an already-closed word to stop immediately instead (treat a `⊣` anywhere in the seed as already-terminated), or is chaining multiple rings from one seed something you want to keep?

Loss looking fine (1.1–1.5, plateaued) is consistent with this — predicting a short trivial sequence token-by-token under teacher forcing is cheap, even though the actual thing it learned to generate is degenerate.

This is the checkpoint from your 10000-step, batch=16, lr=9e-4 run — the one whose loss curve I flagged earlier as plateaued from step ~300 on. That plateau and this collapse are almost certainly the same failure: the run found a low-effort local optimum (spit out `⊢⊣`) and stopped moving.

1	//! p4radice — a transformer whose attention and feed-forward blocks
2	//! never collapse T and F into one number before they've been held.
3	//!
4	//! Source: `ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm
5	//! /dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm_ob3ect.json`, `phases.phase_4.steps`.
6	//! That sequence is not a description of a transformer, it is a build order:
7	//! `∈` split heads, `⊤` affirm arm, `⊥` reject arm, `⊞` HOLD both, `∋` fuse.
8	//! A standard transformer computes `⊤` and `⊥` as one step — masked softmax
9	//! sends the disallowed (future) logits to -inf before the softmax even
10	//! runs, so the "reject" information never exists as a value anywhere. This
11	//! model computes both arms as real tensors, concatenates them (the `⊞`
12	//! hold), and only reduces dimension afterward through a learned projection
13	//! (the `∋` fuse) — so what to do with the contradiction is learned, not
14	//! erased by the architecture in advance.
15	//!
16	//! The feed-forward block repeats the same shape as a two-expert version:
17	//! an affirm expert and a reject expert are BOTH always evaluated (no
18	//! top-1 routing, which would discard one arm the way masked softmax
19	//! discards the future), and a learned gate blends them per token.

# Running p4radice

## Build

```
cargo build --release
```

CUDA build: `cargo build --release --features cuda`

## Train

```
./target/release/p4-train [flags]
./target/release/p4-train --help
```

Nothing is hardcoded — every knob is a flag, all with defaults:

```
  --corpus F        newline-separated glyph rings   (ob3ect_words.txt)
  --out F           checkpoint path                 (p4radice.safetensors)
  --steps n         training steps                  (2000)
  --lr F            AdamW learning rate              (3e-4)
  --batch n         rings per step                   (8)
  --seed n          RNG seed                         (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
  --log-every n     steps between log lines          (100)
  --d-model n       model width                      (64)
  --n-head n        attention heads                  (4)
  --d-ff n          feed-forward width                (256)
  --n-layer n       depth                            (4)
  --max-len n       max sequence length               (128)
```

Example sweep:

```
./target/release/p4-train --d-model 128 --n-head 8 --n-layer 6 --batch 8 --lr 1e-4 --steps 5000 --out big.safetensors
```

The corpus file is newline-separated glyph rings, each built from the twelve
marks. Prints loss and `|W|`/`d|W|` (the weight-norm and its change) every
`--log-every` steps, saves the checkpoint at the end.

## Generate

```
./target/release/p4-gen [flags]
./target/release/p4-gen --help
```

```
  --ckpt F          checkpoint path                  (p4radice.safetensors)
  --seed W          seed word, built from the twelve glyphs   (⊢)
  --n-gen n         glyphs to sample                 (40)
  --d-model / --n-head / --d-ff / --n-layer / --max-len   must match training
```

The five architecture flags are not stored in the `.safetensors` file, so
they must match whatever `p4-train` was run with — a mismatch loads weights
into the wrong-shaped tensors and candle errors on the first size that
disagrees. Samples autoregressively from the seed word until it emits `⊣`
or hits `--n-gen`. Recomputes the full prefix every step — no KV cache yet.

## Vocabulary

Twelve canonical marks: `⊢ ⊣ ≻ ≺ ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ◻`. The on-disk corpus
(`ob3ect_words.txt`) spells AFWD/AREV as retired ASCII `>`/`<` instead of
`≻`/`≺` — `encode()` normalizes those two characters to the canonical marks
on ingest, the same way `imasm_core::lattice_flow::normalize` does for the
kernel, so nothing is silently dropped and nothing gets adopted as a second
alphabet.

## What the architecture does

`src/lib.rs`:

- `DialetheicAttention` — computes an affirm arm (ordinary causal softmax)
  and a reject arm (softmax over exactly the future positions affirm was
  masked from) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head, then
  fuses with one learned projection back to `d_model`. Standard attention
  never computes the reject arm at all — it masks those logits to `-inf`
  before its one softmax runs.
- `DialetheicFfn` — two always-on experts (never top-1 routed) blended by a
  per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side.
- `Block` / `DialetheicLlm` — the usual residual + layernorm stack around
  both, plus token/position embeddings and an output head.

Not built: incremental KV-cache decode (spec step 18). `gen.rs` stands in
for it by recomputing the full sequence each step.

  and a reject arm (softmax over exactly the future positions affirm was
  masked from) as two separate tensors, concatenates them per head, then
  fuses with one learned projection back to `d_model`. Standard attention
  never computes the reject arm at all — it masks those logits to `-inf`
  before its one softmax runs.
- `DialetheicFfn` — two always-on experts (never top-1 routed) blended by a
  per-token sigmoid gate that never fully zeroes either side.
- `Block` / `DialetheicLlm` — the usual residual + layernorm stack around
  both, plus token/position embeddings and an output head.

Not built: incremental KV-cache decode (spec step 18). `gen.rs` stands in
for it by recomputing the full sequence each step.

content.text:
Direct, same-conditions comparison (2000 steps, same corpus, same architecture, only `--gate-lambda` different):

| | control (λ=0) | gated (λ=0.01) | corpus |
|---|---|---|---|
| N (void, e.g. bare `⊢⊣`) | 190 (95%) | 160 (80%) | <1% |
| B (paradox held) | 8 (4%) | 37 (18.5%) | 81% |
| T (clean close) | 2 (1%) | 3 (1.5%) | 18% |
| unique outputs / 200 | 20 | 48 | — |

Connecting the arms was real and it moved the numbers in the right direction — N collapse down 15 points, B up more than 4x, output diversity more than doubled. It also did what the penalty is supposed to do mechanically: `gate` dropped from 0.29 to exactly 0.0000 by step 400 and `|W|` fell from 129 to 108 as the split/fuse weight matrices were pushed toward orthogonality.

It's not fixed, though — 80% N is still collapse, nowhere near the corpus's 81% B. Two honest reads: either 2000 steps isn't enough for the connected arms to actually get used generatively (the penalty reaching exactly 0 that fast suggests the orthogonality constraint was satisfied cheaply, without yet forcing the model to route information through the held structure at inference), or `λ=0.01` is too weak relative to the cross-entropy gradient to matter beyond conditioning the weights. Want me to run it longer at the same λ to see if B keeps climbing, or sweep λ up to see if a stronger pull changes the picture?

content.text:
The actual reason, checked directly against the corpus rather than inferred:

`⊣` does **not** function as a hard terminator in this data. 303 of 1703 rings (17.8%) contain `⊣` somewhere in the middle, not just at the end, and 309 rings (18.1%) don't even end in `⊣` at all. The literal string `⊢⊣` — a 2-glyph ring — appears **zero** times in the entire corpus; the minimum ring length is 3.

`gen.rs` doesn't know any of that. Its stop rule is `if glyph_of(next) == '⊣' { break; }` — the instant it samples a `⊣`, generation halts, no matter where in the sequence that happened. The model correctly learned P(second glyph = `⊣` | first = `⊢`) ≈ 11% from the real data — that's a real, present regularity in the corpus (189 of 1703 rings have `⊣` as their second glyph, then keep going for many more glyphs afterward, since no 2-glyph ring exists). `p4-gen` then takes that entirely normal mid-ring `⊣` and guillotines the output right there, manufacturing `⊢⊣` — a string the training data never once produced — as the single most common thing it prints.

This isn't the model failing to reach for `∈`/`∋`. It's `gen.rs` treating a glyph that's genuinely a mid-ring event 18% of the time as an absolute stop signal 100% of the time. The N-verdict collapse is substantially an artifact of the sampling harness, not a defect in what the model learned.

name = "p4radice"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "Unlicense"

# Built straight from ob3ect/digital/dialetheic_paraconsistent_native_llm's
# phase_4.steps, which is not a description of a transformer but a spec for
# one: multi-head attention that computes an affirm arm (T) and a reject arm
# (F) SEPARATELY, holds both without resolving them to one softmax weight
# (B), and only fuses after that hold. Standard attention throws the reject
# arm away at the masked-softmax step; this keeps it as a real second channel
# and lets a learned projection decide what to do with the contradiction,
# instead of the architecture deciding for it by masking to -inf first.
[dependencies]
candle-core = "0.11"
candle-nn = "0.11"
rand = "0.8"
anyhow = "1"

[features]
default = []
cuda = ["candle-core/cuda", "candle-nn/cuda"]

[lib]
name = "p4radice"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "p4-train"
path = "src/bin/train.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "p4-gen"
path = "src/bin/gen.rs"

content.text:
Enormous shift, same checkpoint, no retraining — only the stop condition changed:

| verdict | before (naive stop-on-⊣) | after (real closure check) | corpus |
|---|---|---|---|
| N | 160 (80%) | **0 (0%)** | <1% |
| B | 37 (18.5%) | **189 (94.5%)** | 81% |
| T | 3 (1.5%) | 7 (3.5%) | 18% |
| F | 0 | 4 (2%) | <1% |
| unique / 200 | 48 | 180 | — |

The model had already learned the corpus's structure. The collapse I reported earlier was a generation-harness artifact — `gen.rs` was guillotining on a glyph that isn't actually a terminator in this data, throwing away everything the model had generated past its first coincidental `⊣`. With the real kernel check gating the stop instead, this checkpoint's output now matches (actually exceeds) the corpus's own 81% B rate.

Updating docs and committing.
